title: Deductible-Decrease Charge on the Risk Premium, NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — the deductible-decrease charge**

*The request billed.* The request billed is the policy's pending deductible-decrease request with no effective date recorded yet, the most recently recorded such request is the one billed, and when it records no loan closing date it is not a request this schedule bills and nothing is charged under it.

*Receipt date.* The premium counts as received on the date of the latest premium payment on the policy when that payment was received on or after the request date, and the receipt date is the later of the request date and that payment date. Where no payment was received on or after the request date, the receipt date is the request date.

*Days of the term.* The days of the current term run from the term start to the term end.

*Effective date.* The change is dated 30 days after the receipt date. Where more than one date applies to the change under this schedule, the change takes effect on the latest of them.

*Rise.* The rise in the full-term risk premium is the request's full-term risk premium (the figure the rating engine returned for the request) less the rated risk premium on the policy.

*The charge.* The deductible-decrease charge on the risk premium is the rise in the full-term risk premium multiplied by the days from the change's effective date to the term end and divided by the days of the current term, rounded half-up to the cent (an amount falling on a half cent, within a tolerance of 0.0001 cent, goes to the higher cent); a change that would take effect after the term end is not charged on this term.

*Reserve fund charge.* The reserve fund charge is booked with the same request and is the tier's Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of the risk premium charge, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Hypothetical worked example** (invented figures, not the record of any policy). A term of 365 days; a request recorded and paid on the same day, which is therefore the receipt date; the change is dated 30 days later, leaving 200 days to the term end. The request's full-term risk premium exceeds the rated risk premium on the policy by 365.00 dollars, so the rise is 365.00. The charge is 365.00 multiplied by 200 and divided by 365, that is 200.00 dollars; at a Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of 18 percent the reserve fund charge is 36.00 dollars. Had the date 30 days after receipt fallen after the term end, nothing would be charged on this term.
